privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.subtitle: Hop has no account. No ads, no advertising trackers, nothing sold.

body.text: No sign-up, no ads, no advertising trackers, no profile of you, and nothing sold. Hop doesn’t send us, or anyone else, your trips, documents or anything you type into it, except what you choose to share. If you email us or join a test version of Hop, we receive what you send us: see “If you live in the UK or EU” below.

Hop is published by Jason Hounsfield through his Apple and Google developer accounts, which are being moved to his company, Hop Group Pty Ltd (trading as Hop Travel). “We” and “us” mean him until then. Contact: support@hoptravelapp.com, or PO Box 193, Australind WA 6233, Australia.

Your chosen passport, your settings and display choices (such as your theme, which tips you’ve already seen and whether Explore shows the map or the list), saved trips, the bookings and places you add to your trips and any confirmations you attach to them, documents you add to a stop or a trip, your notes, your travel history (the countries you’ve been to, with any years and months you add), currency picks and favourites, the last exchange rates Hop downloaded, the latest copy of these legal texts and which version you’ve agreed to, the demo Premium switch, and — if you used an earlier version of Hop — a count of how many separate days you had opened it, are kept in Hop’s own storage on your phone. If you attach a photo or PDF of a visa or approval to a trip stop, or a booking confirmation to a booking, that file is also kept on your phone, in Hop’s own storage. Hop never uploads it or sends it anywhere; it leaves Hop only if you share it or save a copy yourself. When you tap Auto-fill, Hop reads that photo or PDF on your phone to fill in the booking; the file and the words in it never leave your phone. Anyone who can unlock your phone and open Hop, or who can read a backup of your phone, could see it, unless you turn on the optional passcode lock (Settings, Document lock). The lock encrypts the contents of each stored file, including trip documents, with a key made from your passcode; the file’s name, type, size and date stay readable, and the name shows on the locked row. With the lock on, Hop also encrypts your documents, attachments and booking reference numbers. If you turn on Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint unlock, your phone keeps your passcode in its secure storage and releases it only after it recognises you. Hop never receives your face or fingerprint data. The passcode is 4 to 8 digits, so it raises the bar but is not unbreakable, and if you forget it the documents cannot be recovered. Removing a stop, trip or booking deletes its documents and attachments. Countries a trip added to your travel history stay there until you remove them. Deleting the app or clearing its data removes Hop’s copy of everything above, documents included, but not copies in your phone’s backups or files you saved elsewhere. Hop keeps no other copy, so keep your own.

Hop’s screens and information are built into the app, so it works without a connection. When you’re online, Hop downloads a few public data files to keep its information current between app updates: government travel-advisory levels, entry-rule corrections, the dates on which Hop last checked each destination’s entry rules, and the current version of these legal texts. Each comes from raw.githubusercontent.com (GitHub), or from a jsDelivr mirror of the same files if that fails. Hop also fetches exchange rates directly from ExchangeRate-API about once a day, with Frankfurter (European Central Bank rates) as a fallback. Like any web request, these send your IP address and standard technical details to the provider, which handles them under its own privacy policy; Hop adds no personal information, account or identifier to them. Offline, Hop uses the last rates and texts it saved, or the ones built into the app, and makes no requests at all. The Hop website, hoptravelapp.com, is hosted by Cloudflare, which sees routine technical data such as your IP address when you visit. When you open its privacy or terms page, your browser also downloads the current text from GitHub or jsDelivr, which see your IP address.
Hop can send you notifications. They are made on your phone from the same daily data; nothing about you or your trips is sent to Hop.

If you share a trip or your travel map, Hop puts only the details you choose into the link itself, on your phone. Hop doesn’t upload or store them, and the pages at hoptravelapp.com/t/ (trips) and hoptravelapp.com/w/ (travel maps) read the link only in the viewer’s own browser. Anyone who has the link can see those details, and a link can’t be cancelled once sent.

Hop has no analytics: it keeps no count of how often it’s opened or by whom. If you test Hop through Apple’s TestFlight, Apple shows us how many times you’ve used each test build and any crashes, with your name if we invited you by email, or anonymously if you joined through a public link.
Government visa and advisory links open third-party websites with their own privacy practices.

body.lead: If you live in the UK or EU (GDPR).
body.text: The preferences, trips and documents above stay on your phone; we never receive them. If you email us, or join a test version through Apple TestFlight or Google Play, we hold your email address, your name if you give it, your message or feedback, and the TestFlight counts described above, to answer you and run the test (our legitimate interests). Ask support@hoptravelapp.com for a copy, a correction or deletion. The data-file and rate providers receive your IP address when your device contacts them, and handle it under their own privacy policies.
Hop doesn’t ask anyone, including children, for personal information.

We may update this policy without an app update: Hop downloads the current version when you’re online, keeps it for offline use, and shows the date it applies from. If a change is significant, Hop tells you in the app. We keep every earlier version, dated, and will send you a copy if you ask. Questions: support@hoptravelapp.com.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.subtitle: The short version: Hop is a reference, so always confirm before you travel.

body.text: 1. Hop is a personal travel reference tool, currently free, provided as is and as available. It is published by Jason Hounsfield through his Apple and Google developer accounts, which are being moved to his company, Hop Group Pty Ltd (trading as Hop Travel); “we” and “us” mean him until then. Contact: support@hoptravelapp.com.

2. Visa, entry, advisory and currency information may be incomplete, out of date or wrong. You are responsible for confirming all requirements with official government sources, and with your airline, before booking or travelling.

3. Hop is not migration, legal or financial advice, and no agency or advisory relationship is created by using it. Hop is independent and not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any government — see the Disclaimer.

The Australian Consumer Law and the consumer laws of other countries give you rights that no agreement can take away, including guarantees that our services will be supplied with due care and skill. Nothing in these terms excludes, restricts or changes those rights. If we don’t meet a guarantee, you are entitled to the remedies the law provides.
This clause applies only as far as the law allows and never limits your rights under clause 4.

(a) You are responsible for confirming requirements with official sources before you book or travel (clause 2). We are not responsible for loss or costs that happen because you relied on Hop instead of doing that, such as being refused boarding, entry or a visa, or missing travel, unless the loss was caused by our failure to take reasonable care or to meet a consumer guarantee.

(b) We are not responsible for loss caused solely by events outside our reasonable control, such as a government changing its rules or advice without notice, an official website being wrong or unavailable, or a failure of Apple’s, Google’s or a data provider’s systems.
6. Premium in this build is a free demonstration: the unlock is local to your device and no payment is taken. If paid subscriptions launch, these terms will be updated first.

Hop’s own text and design are for your personal, non-commercial use. Photos and government material shown in Hop belong to their owners and are used under their own licences, credited in Settings under Photo credits and Data sources & attribution; those licences, not these terms, govern your use of them. Showing a government’s information does not mean that government endorses Hop.

We may update these terms, the Disclaimer and the Privacy Policy. Hop downloads the current versions when you’re online, so they can change without an app update; each shows the date it applies from, and Hop keeps the last version it downloaded for when you’re offline. A change never applies to anything that happened before its date. If we make an important (“material”) change to these terms or the Disclaimer, Hop shows it to you in the app and asks you to agree before you keep using Hop; if you don’t agree, you can stop using Hop at any time, and you can still open and save your documents. We keep every earlier version, dated, and will send you a copy if you ask.
9. These terms are governed by the laws of Western Australia, Australia.
If you share a trip or your travel map as a link, you choose what it includes, and anyone with the link can see it. A link can’t be cancelled once sent.

body.lead: Hop is a travel reference, not advice.
body.text: It shows general published information about visas, entry rules, travel advisories and currency, plus travel guides, to help you plan. It is not legal, immigration, financial or travel advice, and using Hop creates no advisory relationship.

Rules change, sometimes without notice, and despite careful checking any entry in Hop can be incomplete or out of date. Before you book, and again before you travel, confirm the current requirements with the destination’s embassy, consulate or official immigration website, and with your airline or other carrier, who check travel documents before you board. Every destination card links your own government’s travel advice, and Premium adds a direct link to the destination’s official visa or e-visa portal. “Last date checked” is the last day Hop checked that entry against an official source and found nothing that changes it. It isn’t a promise that the rule hasn’t changed since.

Advisory levels belong to the governments that publish them: Australia, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States. Hop shows each government’s advice on a simple four-step scale. Governments describe their advice in different ways: some use four levels or colours, others use warnings for all or part of a country. Where a government’s own system doesn’t match the scale step for step, the step Hop shows is Hop’s reading of that advice, not the government’s own rating, and the card says so. Always tap through and read the government’s advice itself, including any warnings for parts of a country. For Irish and South Korean passports, Hop links to the government’s travel advice instead of showing a level. India’s government publishes no comparable advisory rating, so Indian passport cards show “No advisory rating”; India’s Ministry of External Affairs may still issue advisories, so check its website too.

Rates are indicative mid-market reference rates. When you’re online, Hop fetches them from ExchangeRate-API about once a day. If that isn’t available, Hop uses the European Central Bank’s reference rates for the currencies they cover and its built-in table for the rest. Offline, Hop uses the last rates it saved or its built-in table, and shows the date of the rates. They are not what a bank, card or money changer will charge you.

Auto-fill reads your tickets and confirmations on your phone and can misread them, and lists you copy from Hop, such as the countries for a visa form, contain only what you’ve recorded. Check them against the originals before you rely on them or put them on a form.
Hop is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by any government or government agency.

Hop is provided as it is, but nothing in this disclaimer limits the guarantees and rights you have under the Australian Consumer Law or other consumer laws. The Terms of Service set out who is responsible for what.
